common_name: White Doves Dwarf Summersweet (Compact Fragrant Clethra)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade to shade; 'White Doves' is a low, dense selection of native summersweet that stays smaller than most cultivars and benefits from steady soil moisture through Gulf Coast summers.

directions: This dwarf selection of the native coastal-plain shrub summersweet forms a tight, rounded mound well under 3 feet, more compact than older cultivars like Hummingbird or Sixteen Candles. In mid- to late summer it sends up dense upright spikes of small, intensely fragrant white flowers that draw bees and butterflies at a time when few other shrubs are blooming. Foliage is clean medium green through the growing season and turns soft yellow in fall before dropping. It tolerates both wet, poorly drained soil and heavier shade than most flowering shrubs, making it a good fit for damp, shaded Gulf Coast beds where larger summersweets would crowd the space.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center

common_name: Chattanooga Dwarf Fothergilla (Compact Bottlebrush Witch Alder)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this unusually compact selection of dwarf fothergilla keeps its tight form and best fall color with some afternoon shade in hot Gulf Coast summers.

directions: Documented in cultivation at the JC Raulston Arboretum, this selection of dwarf fothergilla is noticeably lower and tighter than typical straight-species plants, making it useful where even the already-compact species grows too large. In early spring, honey-scented white bottlebrush flower spikes appear on bare stems before the leaves emerge, drawing in early-season bees. Blue-green summer foliage shifts to a mix of yellow, orange, and red in autumn, often showing several colors on the same leaf at once. It shares the species' preference for acidic, consistently moist soil and performs best along the Gulf Coast with some relief from the hottest afternoon sun.
sources: North Carolina State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox
